paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. Hezekiah gets a letter that says his God can't save him, and he doesn't write back. He takes it up to the house of the LORD and spreads it out before the LORD (2 Kings 19:14). He doesn't hide the problem or pretty it up, because he knows exactly who to hand it to.

Look at how he prays, too. Before he asks for one single thing, he says, "You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth." (2 Kings 19:15). Then he asks to be saved "so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God." (2 Kings 19:19). I think a prayer that starts with who God is looks at a big problem a lot differently than one that starts with the problem.

And God answers. He says, "I have heard your prayer" (2 Kings 19:20), and He keeps His word about Jerusalem (2 Kings 19:32-34). That's the lesson to carry out of my bakery: when something big lands on your counter, spread it out before the LORD and start with who He is. Shouting at the mess never got me anywhere. Hezekiah's story isn't over yet, friend, so keep the oven warm.
